difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that when the second of two composable ring maps is a local complete intersection, the canonical commutative diagram comparing the conormal modules has exact rows and the six-term Jacobi-Zariski sequence can be completed by a zero on the left. The proof reduces the whole statement to the injectivity of one arrow, the map from the conormal module of the first presentation to that of the composed presentation. That injectivity is obtained from the Koszul regularity of the ideal defining the second presentation, which identifies the intersection of the extended ideal with the square of the kernel, and the resulting description of the kernel of the comparison map matches the tensor product expression for the source by right exactness.
